page: The Vultr vbm-32c-755gb-amd is a dedicated bare metal server powered by an AMD EPYC 9354P processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 32 physical cores and 64 threads operating at a base frequency of 3.25 GHz, accompanied by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. It is configured with 768 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, providing a generous allocation of 12 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is provisioned via a bundled 960 GB local SSD, and each deployment includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration hardware.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate exceptional memory throughput and computational execution across demanding enterprise tasks. The platform achieved a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3143.69 and sustained 351.41 GB/s in large-block uncached read operations alongside 165.96 GB/s write bandwidth. Raw processing power is reflected in a stress-ng single-core score of 3179.99 and a multi-core score of 101731.42, complemented by a Geekbench multi-core rating of 20113.0. In synthetic application benchmarks, the server processed 91.34 million Redis SET operations per second and handled text generation for medium 7B parameter language models at 55.29 tokens per second.

With an expansive 768 GB DDR5 memory footprint relative to its 64 vCPUs, the server offers compelling resource density and cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not demand expansive local disk arrays. A notable hardware tradeoff is the bundled storage capacity of 960 GB SSD, which may require external storage scaling for massive data volumes. Consequently, the vbm-32c-755gb-amd is primarily suited for large in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-throughput software compilation pipelines, virtualization hosts, and medium-scale CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: The Vultr vbm-32c-755gb-amd is a dedicated bare metal server engineered for memory-intensive computing workloads. It features an AMD EPYC 9354P processor with 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 3.25 GHz, supported by 768 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 5 GHz and a 960 GB local SSD. Operating without dedicated GPU acceleration, the platform delivers strong compute and top-tier memory benchmark results, achieving 351.41 GB/s in uncached memory reads and handling over 91 million Redis SET operations per second. Its high RAM-to-CPU ratio makes it cost-efficient for workloads requiring large resident memory sets, though secondary storage configurations may be necessary for broad persistent datasets. The hardware profile is optimized for in-memory databases, enterprise caching layers, compilation clusters, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks.
